chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmud, who said:

I said to al-Rida (peace be upon him): 'The tailor or the fuller may be a Jew or a Christian, and you know that he urinates and does not perform ablution (wudu). What is your ruling regarding his work?' He said: 'There is no harm (in it).'

key_terms.الْقَصَّارُ: The fuller (one who cleans and thickens woolen cloth)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on employing non-Muslim artisans who do not perform ablution?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that the ritual impurity (*najasa*) of urine from People of the Book, which they do not purify via ablution, does not invalidate their professional work for Muslims. This ruling underscores the Shia principle of *istihlak* and the general permissibility of employing non-Muslims in trades, distinguishing between their personal ritual status and the validity of their labor contracts. It reflects the practical legal flexibility (*fiqh*) of the Imams in integrating *Ahl al-Kitab* into the socio-economic fabric of early Islamic society.
